title: Authorization
summary: Authorization runs as a pipeline behaviour outside validation, so a request the caller may not make is refused before anything reads data. Rules are requirement classes with their own handlers rather than conditionals in a handler, a request that declares nothing is refused, and every unclear case — unknown policy, missing handler, handler that threw — fails closed.
useWhen: Some requests are not for everyone. Do not check permissions inside a handler, do not write your own current-user abstraction, and do not depend on ASP.NET's authorization for anything a worker or a test also has to enforce.
